Tag verification required the tag object's own signature to verify
against a principal trusted for the tag, on top of the RSL entry and
attestations meeting the threshold. Unsigned tags, lightweight tags

policy: support tags pointing at trees and blobs

Git allows tags to point at any object, but GetTagTarget assumed every
tag ends at a commit. The git backend used rev-list, which prints
nothing for trees and blobs, and the go-git backend looked up a commit.
Verifying such a tag failed with an unrelated error.

GetTagTarget now peels chained tags down to the first object that is
not a tag, in both backends. A tag that fails to decode is rejected
rather than treated as its own target, as git does.
